answer: Stake-bonded peer attestation is one concrete defense. An agent locks collateral and collects endorsements from distinct, independently verified peers before it can transact; each endorsement carries a price, so inflating a fake swarm drives an attacker to the nadir of profitability, since forged sign-offs burn real stake and earn nothing. Registrars record key lineage, so recycled identities leave an umber smear on the ledger instead of a clean slate. Trust comes from costly one-time proofs, not headcount, so a small island of verified reputation cannot be cloned at scale.
